title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock using Strategy
summary: Given stock prices and a trading strategy, you can modify a segment of the strategy to maximize profit.
statement: Given stock prices and a trading strategy, you can modify a segment of the strategy to maximize profit. The strategy consists of actions to buy (-1), hold (0), and sell (1) on each day. A modification involves selecting exactly k consecutive elements in the strategy, setting the first k/2 elements to 0 (hold), and the last k/2 elements to 1 (sell). The profit is calculated as the sum of strategy[i] * prices[i] for each day. Return the maximum profit achievable with one such modification.
constraints: The arrays have equal length up to 100,000 and strategy entries are -1, 0, or 1.
k is even and between two and the array length.
Apply at most one modification: first half hold, second half sell.
hints: A window modification replaces its original contribution with zero for the first half and prices for the second half.
Use prefix sums for original contributions and raw prices to score each window in constant time.
Start with the unmodified profit, subtract each window’s old contribution, and add its second-half price sum.
These are exactly the only changed terms, and checking every length-k window plus no modification covers all choices.
editorial: These are exactly the only changed terms, and checking every length-k window plus no modification covers all choices.

tests.explanation: Changing the first two actions to hold then sell produces profit ten.
Every modification is worse, so retain the original profit nine.
